dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرُّومُ): what history says about them will come in the section on benefits.
(بِضْعِ سِنِينَ): the meaning of biḍʿ and the scholars' disagreement about its number preceded in Sūrat Yūsuf; al-Aṣmaʿī chose that it is from three to ten.

* I'rab:
(الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ): the discussion of the i'rab of (الم) has preceded. (غلبت) is a passive past verb and (الروم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ): (في أدنى) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (غلبت); the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun (من بعد غلبهم) are attached to His saying (سيغلبون); (غلبهم) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the passive verb, annexed to its object; and the clause (سيغلبون) is the predicate of the mubtadaʾ.
(فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ): (في بضع سنين) is also attached to His saying (سيغلبون); the secret of leaving the number of years vague will come in the section on rhetoric. (لله) is a fronted predicate and (الأمر) a postponed subject. The clause is resumptive, as if it were the answer to an implied question, namely: what is the benefit of mentioning His saying (من بعد غلبهم), since His saying (سيغلبون) can only be after the defeat? The answer is that its benefit is to show the completeness of power and to make clear that this is by the command of Allah the Exalted alone. (من قبل) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (من) is a preposition, and (قبل) and (بعد) are two adverbs made indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because they are cut off from annexation in wording [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «لقظا» for «لفظا»] but not in meaning; then they were made genitive by (من) and remained with their ḍamma, i.e. before the defeat of the Romans and after it.
(وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (يفرح), and the tanwīn is a substitute for a clause, as has preceded, i.e. "on the day the Romans overcome"; (بنصر الله) is also attached to (يفرح). The clause (ينصر من يشاء) is resumptive, to show the truthfulness of the believers; (من) is a relative noun, the object of (ينصر), and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) a first predicate and (الرحيم) a second predicate.
(وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): (وعد الله) is a maṣdar emphasizing the content of the preceding clause, namely His saying (سيغلبون) and (ويفرح المؤمنون). The clause (لا يخلف الله وعده) is either explicative, affirming the meaning of the maṣdar, and so has no grammatical position, or a ḥāl from the maṣdar. The wāw is circumstantial; lākinna and its noun, and the clause «لا يعملون» [Translator's note: so in the source, a misprint for «لا يعلمون»] is its predicate.
(يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَهُمْ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ هُمْ غافِلُونَ): concerning the clause (يعلمون), it was said that it is resumptive, and this is a sound view to which there is no objection. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a badal (substitute) from His saying «يعلمون» [Translator's note: so in the source; al-Zamakhsharī's text has «لا يعلمون»]. The subtle point in this substitution is that He substituted it for it and made it such that it takes its place and fills its position, to let you know that there is no difference between the absence of knowledge, which is ignorance, and the presence of a knowledge that does not go beyond this world. His saying (ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا) conveys that this world has an outward and an inward aspect. Its outward aspect is what the ignorant know of enjoying its ornaments and taking pleasure in its delights; its inward aspect and reality is that it is a passage to the Hereafter, from which provision is taken for it through obedience and righteous deeds." Al-Zamakhsharī's view is more firmly rooted in eloquence and fuller of rhetoric, but substituting the affirmative for the negative is not sound, as the rules of grammar stipulate. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن الآخرة) is attached to (غافلون); the second (هم) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first (هم); and (غافلون) is the predicate of the first (هم). The second (هم) may also be a second mubtadaʾ whose predicate is (غافلون), the clause being the predicate of the first (هم).

* Rhetoric:
1- Vagueness (ibhām):
In His saying «في بضع سنين» there is vagueness. Its benefit is magnification, putting fear into the hearts of the polytheists at every moment, and intimating that their pride in themselves and their reliance on their strength last only for a time, long or short, but are bound to come to an end and lead to the inevitable outcome, which is reversal and relapse. Vagueness has been mentioned many times before.
2- Indefiniteness (tankīr):
That is in His saying «يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا». Its benefit is to make what they know small, and making it small brings it close to negation, so that it matches the one substituted for, namely His saying «لا يعلمون». This is what makes the substitution analysis preferable [Translator's note: the source has «البالية», apparently a misprint for «البدلية» (the substitution analysis)]. How excellent al-Zamakhsharī is! How deep his insight and how polished his mind! It is reported from al-Ḥasan that he said, when reciting this verse: "One of them reached such accuracy in the outward life of this world that he would tap the dinar with his finger and know whether it was good or bad." In this there is a diminishing [Translator's note: the source has «تعليل» (giving the reason), apparently a misprint for «تقليل» (diminishing)] of the knowledge which reached its furthest limits, plunged into the depths of the sea, soared into the expanses of space, and perceived the most remote secrets and hidden thoughts; but when it confronts the hidden secrets of the universe, such as the beginning, the return and the final end, it stands insignificant, able neither to begin nor to repeat.
3- Recurrence (taʿaṭṭuf):
In His saying «وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون» there is the device of taʿaṭṭuf, which is the repetition of the very same word within a sentence of speech or a line of poetry. He repeated «هم» for hyperbole in emphasizing their heedlessness of the Hereafter.

* Benefits:
What history says:
(الرُّومُ): a name the Arabs applied to the Byzantines, and which today is applied to the Eastern Melkite Christians, Catholic and Orthodox. The Eastern Roman Empire was known as the Byzantine, after Byzantium, the old name of Constantinople; the Arabs called its inhabitants al-Rūm. The first of the Byzantine emperors — his father Theodosius divided the empire into a western one, with its capital Rome, and an eastern one, with its capital Constantinople [Translator's note: the sentence is incomplete in the source; the emperor's name is not given].
The occasion of the revelation of the verse is that there was fighting between Persia and the Romans. The Romans and Persia fought between Adhriʿāt and Buṣrā, and Persia defeated the Romans. The news reached Mecca, and it grieved the Prophet and the Muslims, because the Persians were Magians with no scripture, while the Romans were People of the Book. The polytheists rejoiced and gloated, and said to the Muslims: "You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, while we are unlettered and the Persians are unlettered; our brothers among the people of Persia have prevailed over your brothers among the Romans, and we shall surely prevail over you." So it was revealed. Abū Bakr said to them: "May Allah not delight your eyes; by Allah, the Romans will surely prevail over Persia after a few years." Ubayy ibn Khalaf said to him: "You lie." Al-Ṣiddīq said to him: "You are the greater liar, O enemy of Allah." He said: "Set a term between us and I will wager with you on it" — al-munāḥaba, with the undotted ḥāʾ, is wagering. So he wagered with him on ten young she-camels from each of them, and they set the term at three years. Abū Bakr informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "That is not what I mentioned; biḍʿ is only between three and nine. So increase the stake and extend the term." So they made it one hundred young she-camels for nine years. When Ubayy ibn Khalaf feared that Abū Bakr would leave, he came to him, held on to him and said: "I fear that you will leave Mecca, so appoint a guarantor for me." His son ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr stood guarantor for him. When Ubayy wanted to go out to Uḥud, ʿAbd Allāh came to him, held on to him and said: "No, by Allah, I will not leave you until you give me a guarantor." So he gave him a guarantor, then went out to Uḥud, then returned to Mecca and died there of the wound which the Prophet had inflicted on him when he fought him in single combat. The Romans prevailed over Persia on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya, and that was at the end of seven years from their wager. Abū Bakr took the stake from Ubayy's heirs and brought it to the Messenger of Allah, who said to him: "Give it in charity." [Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source.]

dervis-irab:30-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حِزْبٍ): al-ḥizb is a group of people; weapons; a man's soldiers and companions who share his opinion; a share; a portion of the Qur'an or of something else. The plural is aḥzāb. Every people whose hearts and deeds resemble one another are aḥzāb, even if they have not met one another.

* I'rab:
(فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ, which discloses an omitted clause). أقم is an imperative verb, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". وجهك is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). للدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقم. حنيفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of أقم, or from its object, or from الدين. (فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْها) It is a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "Cleave to the fiṭra of Allah", meaning His creation. We implied it in the address to a plural audience because of what comes later, منيبين إليه, as will follow. It was also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb, i.e. "He created you with a creation (faṭarakum fiṭratan)". التي is an adjective (naʿt) of الفطرة, the clause فطر الناس is the ṣila (relative clause), and عليها is attached to فطر. (لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ) The sentence gives the reason for the command to cleave to His fiṭra. لا is the lā of generic negation, تبديل is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and لخلق الله is the predicate. (ذلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) ذلك is the subject (mubtadaʾ), الدين its predicate (khabar), and القيم an adjective. The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive. ولكن is lākinna with its noun, and the clause لا يعلمون is its predicate. (مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَلا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) منيبين is a ḥāl from the implied agent of الزموا, as we indicated above; this is better than making it a ḥāl from the agent of أقم. واتقوا الله is conjoined to the implied الزموا, and likewise the words وأقيموا الصلاة. لا is prohibitive, تكونوا is an imperfect defective verb (kāna), jussive by the prohibitive lā, and the wāw is its noun, and من المشركين is its predicate. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ وَكانُوا شِيَعاً) من الذين is a badal (substitute) for the words من المشركين, with repetition of the governing particle. The clause فرقوا دينهم is the ṣila. وكانوا شيعا: kāna, its noun and its predicate. (كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ) كل حزب is the subject; بما is attached to فرحون; the adverbial لديهم is attached to an omitted element forming the ṣila of the relative noun; and فرحون is the predicate of كل. The sentence is explicative, confirming what precedes.

dervis-irab:33-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُلْطاناً): al-sulṭān is proof (ḥujja); you say "he has a clear sulṭān", i.e. clear proof; it also means kingship. The wording of al-Qāmūs is: "al-sulṭān is proof and the power of kingship, and its lām takes ḍamma; and the ruler. It is feminine because it is the plural of salīṭ, for the oil, as if it illuminated; or kingship, or because it means proof; and it may be treated as masculine, going by the sense of 'man'." And in al-Asās: "He has authority over them", "and I had no authority over you" ... "he has a clear sulṭān": a proof. "Sanābik sulṭāt" means long hooves. Al-Jaʿdī said, describing a horse:
مدلّا على سلطات النسو ... رشمّ السنابك لم تقلب
(Roughly: "Confident upon long-hoofed legs, with hooves marked, never turned back.") And he anointed its lamp-wick with salīṭ, which is good oil." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "al-sulṭān is treated as masculine because it means evidence (dalīl), and as feminine because it means proof (ḥujja); it was also said that it is the plural of salīṭ, like raghīf, pl. rughfān." (يَقْنَطُونَ): they despair of mercy. In al-Miṣbāḥ: it is with fatḥa or kasra on the nūn, both being among the seven readings, and its pattern is ḍaraba and taʿiba. In al-Qāmūs: "qaniṭa like naṣara, ḍaraba, ḥasiba and karuma, verbal noun qunūṭ, and like fariḥa, verbal noun qanaṭ and qanāṭa, and like manaʿa and ḥasiba (these two combine the two dialects): he despaired, so he is qaniṭ like fariḥ; and qannaṭahu taqnīṭan: he made him despair. Al-qanṭ is also withholding, and the raisins of a child." [Translator's note: the source text of this lexical quotation is slightly garbled and its wording is rendered as written.]

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا مَسَّ النَّاسَ ضُرٌّ دَعَوْا رَبَّهُمْ مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to depict the fickle nature of people and their wavering between hope and despair. إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause مس is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. الناس is a fronted direct object, and ضر a postponed agent. The clause دعوا ربهم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ربهم is a direct object, منيبين is a ḥāl from the agent of دعوا, and إليه is attached to منيبين. (ثُمَّ إِذا أَذاقَهُمْ مِنْهُ رَحْمَةً إِذا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ) ثم is a conjunction of order and delay. إذا is conditional, and the clause أذاقهم is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. منه is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of رحمة; رحمة is the second direct object. إذا is the sudden إذا (al-fujāʾiyya), which links the apodosis of the first إذا to its condition, so it takes the place of the fāʾ in linking. فريق is the subject, منهم an adjective, بربهم is attached to يشركون, and the clause يشركون is the predicate.
(لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) The lām denotes reason, or consequence and outcome; it was also said that it is the lām of command, the intended sense of the command being threat and warning. يكفروا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām. بما is attached to يكفروا, and the clause آتيناهم is the ṣila. فتمتعوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and تمتعوا is an imperative verb in which there is a shift from the third person to the second person (iltifāt), to be emphatic in rebuking them; and the fāʾ occurs in the response to the command. سوف is a particle of futurity, and تعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw its agent. (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِما كانُوا بِهِ يُشْرِكُونَ) أم is a disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction, so it has the sense of "rather" (bal). أنزلنا is a verb and its agent, عليهم is attached to أنزلنا, and سلطانا is a direct object. The fāʾ is a conjunction, هو is the subject, and the clause يتكلم is the predicate. بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتكلم, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila. It is also permissible that ما be a maṣdar, with kāna and its noun, and به attached to يشركون, and the clause يشركون the predicate of كانوا.
(وَإِذا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً فَرِحُوا بِها) Conjoined to what precedes. The clause فرحوا بها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and the clause أذقنا is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ) Also conjoined. تصبهم is the protasis, سيئة is the agent, the bāʾ is causal, and ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تصبهم, and the clause قدمت has no position. إذا is the sudden إذا, which has taken the place of the fāʾ in linking the apodosis to the condition; هم is the subject, and the clause يقنطون is the predicate; and the clause إذا هم يقنطون is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ) The hamza is for rhetorical interrogation conveying affirmation, and the wāw is conjoined to an omitted element that the context requires. لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussion, and يروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم. أن and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of يروا; أن and its noun, and the clause يبسط الرزق is its predicate. لمن is attached to يبسط, the clause يشاء is the ṣila, and يقدر is conjoined to يبسط. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) The i'rab of its like has been given many times before.

* Rhetoric:
In His words (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ) there is a rational figurative usage (majāz ʿaqlī), as when you say "his book speaks of such-and-such". This is among what the Qur'an has itself expressed with "speaking"; its meaning is indication and testimony, so it testifies to their polytheism, or to that which they associate (with Allah).

dervis-irab:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(فَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبى حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses an omitted clause whose implied form is "if you have come to know that the evil befell them because of what their hands have forwarded, then give". آت is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". ذا القربى is the first direct object and حقه the second direct object. Abū Ḥanīfa has cited this verse as proof of the obligation of maintenance for close relatives (maḥārim) when they are needy and unable to earn, whereas al-Shāfiʿī drew an analogy between relatives and the cousin, since there is no direct parentage between them. والمسكين is conjoined to ذا القربى, and likewise ابن السبيل.
(ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) ذلك is the subject and خير the predicate. للذين is attached to خير, the clause يريدون is the ṣila with the wāw as agent, and وجه الله is a direct object, i.e. His reward. أولئك is the subject, هم a second subject, and المفلحون the predicate of هم, and the sentence is the predicate of أولئك. (وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ فَلا يَرْبُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is conditional, in the position of the accusative as a fronted direct object of آتيتم; آتيتم is a verb and its agent; من ربا is a ḥāl. In ليربوا the lām denotes reason, and يربوا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to آتيتم. في أموال الناس is attached to يربوا; the sense of containment (ẓarfiyya) will come in the chapter on rhetoric. The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition, لا is negative, and يربوا is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. عند الله is attached to يربوا. (وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ زَكاةٍ تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُضْعِفُونَ) Conjoined to what precedes. The meaning of His words فأولئك هم المضعفون is: those who have multiples of reward. The secret of the shift in person (iltifāt) will come in the chapter on rhetoric.
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ رَزَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ) الله is the subject, and الذي خلقكم is its predicate; the clause خلقكم is the ṣila, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ مِنْ ذلِكُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ سُبْحانَهُ وَتَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ) هل is an interrogative particle, and من شركائكم is a fronted predicate, with من partitive. من يفعل is a postponed subject. من ذلكم is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl from شيء because it was originally an adjective of it. من is a redundant preposition (zāʾida) and شيء is genitive in form by من, and in position a direct object of يفعل; it was made redundant for it because an indefinite noun within an interrogative that contains the sense of negation (takes it). سبحانه is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb, تعالى is a past verb, عما is attached to تعالى, and ما is a maṣdar or a relative.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metonymy (kināya):
In His words «ليربوا في أموال الناس» there is a metonymy, because the increase that the usurer takes from people's wealth is not his property at all; so the containment (ẓarfiyya) is the locus of the metonymy.
2- Shift of person (iltifāt):
In His words «فأولئك هم المضعفون» there is a shift from the second person to the third for the sake of exaltation; it is more laudatory than saying "so you are the ones who multiply". It also contains the omission of the direct object, i.e. their reward.

dervis-irab:41-45.t:
* I'rab:
(ظَهَرَ الْفَسادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to affirm the corruption, wrong, diversion and play, and everything else called corruption, which is the opposite of soundness, that has spread throughout the various regions of land and sea. ظهر الفساد is a verb and agent; في البر والبحر is attached to ظهر, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl, which is perhaps more likely; and بما is attached to ظهر, i.e. because of their earning, in which case ما is a maṣdar, or because of that which they earned, in which case it is a relative. أيدي الناس is the agent of كسبت. (لِيُذِيقَهُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) The lām is the lām of reason, and يذيقهم is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن. It is preferable that the preposition and its genitive noun be attached to an omitted element, i.e. "He punished them with that". It was also said that the lām is not for reason but for consequence, because that is their end and outcome; and Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be attached to ظهر. The hāʾ is the first direct object of يذيق, and بعض الذي عملوا is its second object. لعل and its noun, and the clause يرجعون is its predicate. (قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ) The clause سيروا في الأرض is the content of the saying. فانظروا is conjoined to سيروا. كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted predicate of كان; kāna and its noun, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of انظروا, which is suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative. من قبل is attached to an omitted element forming the ṣila of الذين. (كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُشْرِكِينَ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to explain that what befell them was due to the prevalence of polytheism among most of them, and of corruption and disobedience among the fewer. (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ الْقَيِّمِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; أقم is an imperative verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", referring to the Messenger ﷺ, the intended meaning being his community. وجهك is a direct object, للدين is attached to أقم, and القيم is an adjective of الدين, i.e. make your direction the following of the upright religion, of utmost straightness; the explanation of this word has been given before.
(مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ) من قبل is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, and أن and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar in the genitive by annexation. يوم is the agent of يأتي. لا is the lā of generic negation, مرد its noun, and له its predicate, and the sentence is an adjective of يوم. As for من الله, you may attach it to يأتي, i.e. "there comes from Allah a day which none can turn back", and you may attach it to an omitted element indicating the maṣdar formed from أن and "turning it back"; but it is not permissible to attach it to مرد, because it would then resemble a muḍāf (genitive construct) and would be declined. يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to يصدعون, and the tanwīn is a substitute for a sentence. يصدعون is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been omitted, i.e. they will separate, on the day when this day comes. It is said "the people taṣaddaʿa" when they scatter; hence ṣudāʿ (headache), because it splits the branches of the head. The poet said:
وكنا كندماني جذيمة حقبة ... من الدهر حتى قيل لن يتصدعا
(We were like the two drinking-companions of Jadhīma for a span of time, until it was said they would never part.)
(مَنْ كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ وَمَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً فَلِأَنْفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ) The sentence is explicative, with no grammatical position, introduced to explain His words يصدعون. من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as subject; كفر is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ links the apodosis; عليه is a fronted predicate and كفره a postponed subject; the sentence is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the predicate of من. ومن عمل صالحا is conjoined to what precedes, parallel to it in i'rab. As for صالحا, it may be a direct object or an adjective of a maṣdar, i.e. "righteous work". The fāʾ links, ولأنفسهم is attached to يمهدون, and the sentence is the apodosis of the condition, i.e. they prepare their soft beds and level them lest they jolt them so that their sleeping places become uneven and their life turns bitter. (لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْكافِرِينَ) The lām denotes reason, and يجزي is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يمهدون, or to يصدعون, or to an omitted predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "that is so in order that He may reward". الذين is the object of يجزي, the clause آمنوا is the ṣila, and عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila. من فضله is attached to يجزي. إن and its noun, and the clause لا يحب is its predicate, and الكافرين is a direct object. The sentence has no grammatical position, because it is causal.

* Rhetoric:
In His words (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ الْقَيِّمِ) there is jinās al-munāsaba (paronomasia of affinity) in the wording, because jinās has two origins, jinās al-muzāwaja and jinās al-munāsaba; this has been fully covered before.

dervis-irab:46-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرِّياحَ): one of the plurals of ريح (wind). Rīḥ is feminine and is also pluralised as arwāḥ, aryāḥ and rīḥ, and the plural of the plural is arāwīḥ and arāyīḥ. The winds (riyāḥ) are four:
the south wind (janūb), which is the qibla wind; the north wind (shamāl), which is the northern one; the east wind (ṣabā), which is the eastern one; and the west wind (dabūr), which is the western one. The first three are winds of mercy and the fourth is the wind of punishment. It was mentioned before that the word ريح (singular) never occurs in the Qur'an except in the context of evil, while the plural occurs in the context of good. From this we see that Arabic is rich in its signification, and that if we delve into the words specialised for particular matters, we derive understandings that perhaps we pay no heed to in our modern writing.
(كِسَفاً): with kasra then fatḥa; it is also permissible to put sukūn on the sīn. It is the plural of kisfa, i.e. a piece. In al-Qāmūs: "al-kisfa, with kasra, is a piece of a thing; the plural is kisaf and kusaf, and the plural of the plural is aksāf and kusūf; kasafahu yaksifuhu: he cut it."
(الْوَدْقَ): rain.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ الرِّياحَ مُبَشِّراتٍ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to present His signs, Exalted is He. ومن آياته is a fronted predicate, and أن and what falls within its scope is a postponed subject. الرياح is a direct object and مبشرات a ḥāl. This is the first purpose of sending them.
(وَلِيُذِيقَكُمْ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَلِتَجْرِيَ الْفُلْكُ بِأَمْرِهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to His word مبشرات, because the ḥāl and the adjective alternate in conveying the reason, so that the implied sense is "to give you good tidings and to let you taste". The wording of al-Zamakhsharī in this regard: "If you ask: to what is وليذيقكم attached? I say: there are two possibilities: that it is conjoined to مبشرات by sense, as if it had been said 'to give you good tidings and to let you taste'; and that it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being 'and in order that He may let you taste, and in order that such-and-such be so, We sent them'." من رحمته is attached to يذيقكم, and the meaning of this figurative usage will come in the chapter on rhetoric. ولتجري الفلك is also a conjunction; بأمره is a ḥāl; ولتبتغوا من فضله is also a conjunction; ولعلكم تشكرون: laʿalla and its noun, and the clause تشكرون is its predicate.
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ رُسُلًا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ فَجاؤُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ) [Translator's note: in the source the opening parenthesis and the verse text are garbled by a stray diacritic; the verse is rendered as intended.] A resumptive sentence, introduced to console him ﷺ, to comfort him and to announce victory. The lām is the one that prepares for an oath, قد is a particle of certainty, أرسلنا is a verb and agent, من قبلك is a ḥāl, رسلا is a direct object, and إلى قومهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا. فجاؤوهم is conjoined to أرسلنا, and بالبينات is attached to جاؤوهم or to an omitted element as a ḥāl. (فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا وَكانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, the implied form being "so they denied them, so We took vengeance". من الذين is attached to انتقمنا, and the clause أجرموا is the ṣila. وكان: the wāw is resumptive, kāna is a defective past verb, حقا is its fronted predicate, and علينا is attached to حقا or to an omitted element as its adjective, and نصر المؤمنين is its postponed noun. This is the straightforward i'rab. Some of the parsers went to some length and allowed that حقا is a maṣdar and علينا the predicate, and that there is a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in kāna, حقا being a maṣdar, and علينا نصر being a subject and predicate in the position of the accusative as the predicate of kāna. In this speech there is a magnification of the matter of the believers, a qualifying of them for honour and for deserving reward and victory; and in the definiteness of المؤمنين there is an acclaim of them and an allusion that whoever falls short of their ranks does not deserve this greatest favour. (اللَّهُ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّياحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحاباً فَيَبْسُطُهُ فِي السَّماءِ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ) Also a resumptive sentence, to detail what was summarised in mentioning the winds and their states. الله is the subject and الذي its predicate, the clause يرسل الرياح is the ṣila, فتثير is conjoined to يرسل, and سحابا is a direct object; the fāʾ is a conjunction, and يبسطه is also conjoined to تثير, and في السماء is attached to يبسطه. كيف is a particle of condition and suspension, as in their saying "how you act, I act" and "how you are, I am", except that it does not make the verb jussive; its apodosis is omitted because what precedes it indicates it, as is the object of يشاء. It has been said before that the object after يشاء is mostly omitted, the implied form being "how He wills its spreading, He spreads it"; so "its spreading" was omitted because it is the object of يشاء, and "He spreads it" was omitted because the first يبسطه indicates it. كيف is accusative as a ḥāl of the verb after it, and the meaning is: in whatever state He wills to spread it, He spreads it. A further discussion of the conditional كيف will come in the chapter on benefits. (وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلالِهِ) ويجعله is conjoined to يبسطه; the hāʾ is the first object of يجعل and كسفا is its second object. فترى is conjoined to what precedes, the agent of ترى is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", الودق is a direct object, and the clause يخرج is circumstantial because the seeing here is by sight; من خلاله is attached to يخرج.
(فَإِذا أَصابَ بِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ إِذا هُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause أصاب is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. به is attached to أصاب, and من يشاء is the object of أصاب, and من عباده is a ḥāl. إذا is the sudden إذا, occurring in the apodosis of the first إذا; هم is the subject and the clause يستبشرون is the predicate. (وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction. إن is the lightened form of the heavy inna, either idle or operating on an omitted pronoun of the matter; kāna and its noun; من قبل is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; أن and what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar annexed to قبل; ينزل is a passive imperfect verb subjunctive by أن, عليهم is attached to it, and the deputy agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it". The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and مبلسين is its predicate. As for the second من قبله, it was said to be a repetition and emphasis of the first من قبل. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It belongs to the chapter of repetition and emphasis, like His words «فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها». The meaning of emphasis here is to indicate that their last experience of rain had become long ago and distant, so that their despair became firm and their dejection prolonged, so the rejoicing was in proportion to their distress at that." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The benefit of this emphasis is to announce how quickly human hearts turn from dejection to rejoicing. That is because His words 'before it was sent down upon them' allow for a span of time, i.e. before it came down in abundance, so His words 'before it' came to mean that this is directly connected with the rain; so it is a useful emphasis."
(فَانْظُرْ إِلى آثارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you wish to know what follows upon the sending down of the rain, then look". انظر is an imperative verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; إلى آثار رحمة الله is attached to انظر; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and it is suspended (muʿallaqa) so that انظر does not operate; الأرض is a direct object; بعد موتها is an adverbial attached to يحيي; and the sentence is a badal (substitute) of آثار, so it is in the scope of the accusative by removal of the preposition. The meaning is: after all this, look at His wondrous giving of life to the earth after its death; the intention is to draw attention to the greatness of His power and the breadth of His mercy. (إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَمُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) inna and its noun, i.e. "that Powerful One"; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and محيي الموتى is its predicate. هو is the subject, على كل شيء is attached to قدير, and قدير is the predicate of هو.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «وليذيقكم من رحمته» there are an isti'āra (metaphor) and a majāz (figurative usage). The isti'āra is in His words ليذيقكم, and it has been mentioned many times; it is an isti'āra makniyya (implicit metaphor). The majāz mursal (free figure) is in His words من رحمته; it is a majāz mursal whose relation is "that which occupies" (ḥāliyya), because mercy resides in fertility and rain, so the occupant was named and the locus intended. Some explained "mercy" by saying: "i.e. from His bounty of sweet waters, fresh trees, bodily health, and whatever follows from that, matters which none can count but Allah."

* Benefits:
Kayfa again:
In al-Mughnī it is stated verbatim: "It is used in two ways. One is that it be conditional, in which case it requires two verbs agreeing in wording and meaning, not jussive, such as 'how you act, I act'. It is not permitted, by agreement, to say 'how you sit, I go', nor 'how you sit, I sit' with the jussive, according to the Basrans, except Quṭrub, because it differs from the conditional particles in the necessity that its apodosis agree with its protasis, as has passed. It was also said that it is permitted absolutely, and that is the view of Quṭrub and the Kufans; and it was said that it is permitted on condition that it be joined with mā. They said: among its occurrences as a conditional are «ينفق كيف يشاء», «يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء», «فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء», and its apodosis in all of that is omitted because what precedes it indicates it. This poses a difficulty for their general claim that its apodosis must match its protasis." Some of the commentators have made a supplementary remark on al-Mughnī, saying: "Some answered that it is possible to imply the apodosis agreeing with the protasis, by implying the apodosis as the act of His will connected with the preceding verb, which indicates it, because a voluntary act necessitates will; the original being 'how He wills a matter, He wills the shaping in the wombs', 'how He wills a matter, He wills the spending', 'how He wills a matter, He wills its spreading'; the most that can be said is that what the two verbs relate to is different. This is a far-fetched answer, because they said 'because what precedes it indicates it', and what comes to mind is that it indicates the apodosis, and a removal of the difficulty; so what precedes it would indicate what the apodosis relates to, not the apodosis itself. And you have known the rebuttal of this: that the voluntary act, which is the act occurring before it, necessitates the will, and that is the omitted apodosis."

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is a conjunction attached to an implied clause required by the context; لم is a particle of negation, reversal (of tense) and jussive; يتفكروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, the wāw is fāʿil (agent); في أنفسهم is attached to يتفكروا; ما is negative; خلق الله السموات is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, having no connection with what precedes. It is also said that it is in the position of accusative, suspended from the thinking (taʿlīq), so it would be in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition. إلا is a particle of restriction, and بالحق is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by the truth". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The bāʾ in 'إلا بالحق' is like the bāʾ in your saying 'I entered upon him in travelling clothes' and 'he bought the horse with its saddle and bridle', meaning he bought it while it was joined with the saddle and bridle, not separated from them. Likewise the meaning is: He did not create them except while they were joined with the truth, accompanied by it." أجل is conjoined to الحق, and مسمى is an adjective (naʿt) of أجل. (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكافِرُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إنّ and its ism; من الناس is an adjective of كثيرا; بلقاء ربهم is attached to كافرون; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and كافرون is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. (أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) The hamza is for rebuking, reproving interrogation, and the wāw is a conjunction attached to an implied clause required by the context, i.e. "Did they sit in their places and not travel?"; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يسيروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, the wāw is fāʿil; في الأرض is attached to يسيروا; فينظروا: the fāʾ is a conjunction attached to يسيروا, and you may take the fāʾ as causal (sabab), with ينظروا an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a fronted khabar of كان; عاقبة is its ism; الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and من قبلهم is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.
(كانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَثارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوها أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوها) The clause كانوا is either explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position, or you may take it as a following clause by way of substitution (badal). كان and its ism, and أشد is its khabar; منهم is attached to أشد, and قوة is tamyīz (specification); وأثاروا الأرض is conjoined to كانوا, and وعمروها is also conjoined, being a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; أكثر is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a cultivation greater than their cultivation"; مما is attached to أكثر, and ما is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun forming), interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar governed by the genitive من. (وَجاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ) وجاءتهم رسلهم: a verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil; بالبينات is attached to جاءتهم; the fāʾ is a conjunction, ما is negative, كان and its ism; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and يظلمهم is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar, whose explanation has already preceded. ولكن: the wāw is circumstantial, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) that does not operate; كانوا is a past defective verb and the wāw is its ism; أنفسهم is a fronted mafʿūl of يظلمون, and the clause يظلمون is the khabar of كانوا. (ثُمَّ كانَ عاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أَساؤُا السُّواى) ثم: the fāʾ (sic) is a conjunction of delay and of commencing the statement of their destruction in the Hereafter after their destruction in the world; كان is a past defective verb, and عاقبة is the fronted khabar of كان; الذين is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause أساءوا is the ṣila; السوءى is an adjective of the maṣdar of أساءوا. [Translator's note: the source says "ثم الفاء" (thumma, the fāʾ); read as written, thumma is the conjunction.]
(أَنْ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَكانُوا بِها يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) أن and what is within its scope is the delayed ism of كان; and you may make السوءى the ism, with أن and what is within its scope accusative by removal of the preposition, or a substitute (badal) of السوءى. What follows is the text of Abū al-Baqāʾ's i'rab, which is the clearest of the analyses: "His saying, Exalted: 'ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوءى' is read with nominative and accusative. Whoever put it in the nominative made it the ism of كان, and for the khabar there are two possibilities: one, السوءى, with أن كذبوا in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. 'because they denied' or 'by their denying', or in the position of genitive with the preposition implied, according to al-Khalīl's view; the second, that أن كذبوا is the khabar, i.e. 'the end of their affair was denial', and السوءى on this reading is an adjective of a maṣdar. Whoever put it in the accusative made it the khabar of كان, and for the ism there are two possibilities: one, السوءى, and the other أن كذبوا, as above; and it is permissible to make أن كذبوا a substitute of السوءى or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. السوءى is of the pattern فعلى from الأسوأ and is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being 'أساء الإساءة السوءى'. If you make it an ism or a khabar, the implied form is 'الفعلة السوءى' or 'العقوبة السوءى'."
وكانوا: كان and its ism; بها is attached to يستهزئون, and the clause يستهزئون is the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:11-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُبْلِسُ): أبلس فلان, so he is مبلس, when he falls silent out of despair. It is said: أبلس الرجل, his argument was cut off and he fell silent; it is intransitive and does not take an object. In al-Kashshāf: "الإبلاس is to remain silent, despairing, bewildered. One says 'I disputed with him and he was ablasa', if he did not utter a word and despaired of arguing; from it is the she-camel المبلاس that does not groan." In the Qāmūs: "وأبلس: he despaired and was bewildered, and from it is Iblīs, or it is non-Arabic (aʿjamī)." So the statement of the author of al-Munjid that one says "أبلسه" is a gross error. The scholars of morphology explained the reading يبلس, with the passive, by saying that the word standing in the place of the agent is the verbal noun of the verb, then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, since the original is "يبلس إبلاس المجرمين".
(رَوْضَةٍ): الروضة: any land with vegetation, water, brilliance and freshness. Among their proverbs: "Finer than an egg in a روضة", meaning an ostrich egg. In al-Asās and al-Lisān: "In his land there is a روضة, and روضات and رياض; and the rain made the land a meadow (روّض), and the place became a meadow (أراض), and استراض, i.e. its meadows became many. Figuratively: 'I am with you in a روضة and a stream', and 'your assembly is a روضة from the meadows of Paradise'."
(يُحْبَرُونَ): They are made glad. One says حبره when he gladdened him with a joy at which his face beamed and whose trace is in it. In al-Asās: "And حبره Allah: He gladdened him; 'فهم في روضة يحبرون'; and he is محبور: glad." Ibn al-Rūmī said describing grapes:
ثم جلسنا مجلس المحبور ... على حفافي جدول مسجور
(Then we sat in the seat of the delighted, on the two banks of an overflowing stream.)
In al-Kashshāf: "The sayings about it then differed because it admits the aspects of all kinds of delights. On the authority of Mujāhid (may Allah be pleased with him): they are honoured; on the authority of Qatāda: they are pampered; on the authority of Ibn Kaysān: they are adorned; on the authority of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh: crowns on their heads; on the authority of Wakīʿ: listening to song (samāʿ) in Paradise. And on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ that he mentioned Paradise and the bliss in it, and at the back of the people was a bedouin, who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there samāʿ in Paradise?' He said: 'Yes, O bedouin. In Paradise there is a river with virgins on both its banks, every fair, slender-waisted one, who sing in voices the like of which creation has never heard; that is the best of the bliss of Paradise.' The narrator said: I asked Abū al-Dardāʾ: 'What do they sing?' He said: 'Glorification (tasbīḥ).' It is related that in Paradise there are trees with silver bells on them; when the people of Paradise wish for samāʿ, Allah sends a wind from beneath the Throne which falls on those trees and moves those bells with sounds which, if the people of this world heard them, they would die of rapture." Further, a pleasant section on samāʿ and its effect will come in the chapter on benefits.

* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ) The majestic name is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يبدأ الخلق is its khabar (predicate); ثم يعيده is conjoined to يبدأ. (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ) The adverb is attached to يبلس, and the clause تقوم is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; الساعة is fāʿil (agent) of تقوم, and يبلس المجرمون is a verb and fāʿil. (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ مِنْ شُرَكائِهِمْ شُفَعاءُ وَكانُوا بِشُرَكائِهِمْ كافِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive, يكن is an imperfect defective verb jussive by لم, and لهم is the fronted khabar of يكن; ومن شركائهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) because it was originally an adjective of شفعاء and was fronted before it; شفعاء is the ism of يكن; وكانوا: كان and its ism; بشركائهم is attached to كافرين, and كافرين is the khabar of كانوا. (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ) The adverb is attached to يتفرقون; the i'rab of its like has already preceded; and يومئذ is a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of the adverb. (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَهُمْ فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ) The fāʾ is a fāʾ of consequence (tafrīʿiyya); أما is a particle of condition and elaboration; الذين is mubtadaʾ, the clause آمنوا is the ṣila, and the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila; the fāʾ is a connector because of the scent of condition in the relative noun; هم is mubtadaʾ, في روضة is attached to يحبرون, and the clause يحبرون is the khabar of هم, and the sentence is the khabar of الذين.
(وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَلِقاءِ الْآخِرَةِ فَأُولئِكَ فِي الْعَذابِ مُحْضَرُونَ) Conjoined to the preceding sentence and its like in i'rab; the meaning of محضرون is that they are not absent from it, and it is not lightened for them.

* Benefits:
Song in Paradise and the song of the houris:
It is related on the authority of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'In Paradise there is a gathering place for the houris, who raise voices the like of which creation has never heard, saying: We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the blissful, so we shall not suffer; we are the content, so we shall not be angry. Blessed is he who is ours and for whom we are.'"
And on the authority of Abū Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "In Paradise there is a river the length of Paradise, with maidens standing opposite one another on its two banks, singing in the most beautiful voices that creation hears, so that they do not think there is a pleasure in Paradise like it. We said: O Abū Hurayra, and what is that song? He said: If Allah wills, it is glorification (tasbīḥ), praise (taḥmīd), sanctification (taqdīs) and extolling of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic."
A glimpse of the history of song:
In past ages song was not as we know it today, with fixed rules and bonds, but was simple. The first to set rules and regulations for it, as is said, was Ptolemy, a mathematician-philosopher who occupied himself with mathematics and music, and to him is ascribed the first musical scale. The first among the Arabs to sing, of women, were two singing girls of ʿĀd called al-Jarādatān (the two locusts), and part of their singing was:
ألا يا قين ويحك قم وهينم ... لعل الله يصبحنا غماما
(O Qayn, woe to you, rise and murmur a prayer; perhaps Allah will give us the morning with clouds.)
The first among men to sing in Yemen was Dhū Jadan, who was a qayl (petty king) of the qayls of Ḥimyar. Thus the singing of the Arabs in their pre-Islamic days was simple, like the chanting of camel-drivers in their ḥudāʾ for their camels, and of youths about the moon, the star, the wilderness and the horses. Song is mentioned in their poetry; Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
إذا نحن قلنا: اسمعينا انبرت لنا ... على رسلها مطروفة لم تردّد
(When we said "let us hear you", she set about it for us at her leisure, lowering her gaze, without hesitating.)
that is, without affectation; and his word مطروفة is the one whose eye-edge (ṭarf) has been struck by something, i.e. as though her eye-edge was struck because of the languor of her glance; it is also transmitted مطلوقة and مطروقة.
Ibn Rashīq al-Qayrawānī said in the book al-ʿUmda: "The song of the Arabs anciently was of three kinds: al-naṣb, al-sinād and al-hazaj. As for al-naṣb, it is the song of riders and youths. Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm said: it is what is called al-mirāʾī, and it is the Janābī song, which a man of Kalb called Janāb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubal derived, and it was ascribed to him; from it was the origin of the ḥudāʾ, and all of it comes out of the original of al-ṭawīl in prosody. As for al-sinād, it is the heavy (thaqīl) with much trilling, many melodies and accents, and it is of six modes: the first heavy and its light form, the second heavy and its light form, and the ramal and its light form. As for al-hazaj, it is the light, to which one dances and walks with the tambourine and the flute, so it delights and makes the forbearing light-headed.
Isḥāq said: This was the song of the Arabs until Allah brought Islam, and Iraq was conquered and delicate song was imported from Persia and Byzantium, and they sang the divided, composed song in Persian and Greek, and all sang with lutes, tanbūrs, ʿazf instruments and flutes.
Al-Jāḥiẓ said: The Arabs cut up measured melodies to fit measured poems, while the non-Arabs stretch the words, contracting and expanding them until they enter the measure of the melody, thereby placing something measured upon something not measured.
They remained on this way of theirs until Islam came; at that time they were moved only by recitation and martial poetry, because of the hold of religion on them and because they were in a period of founding and conquests. When matters became settled for them, ease and luxury came to dominate them and they inclined to repose, their natures grew tender and their sides soft; and the singers from among the Persians and Byzantines dispersed and came to the Ḥijāz and became their clients, and all sang with lutes, tanbūrs and ʿazf instruments, and the Arabs heard their melodizing of voices and set their poems to those tunes.
The effect of song:
Al-Ghazālī said in al-Iḥyāʾ: "Allah has a secret in the correspondence of measured melodies to the spirits, so that they affect them wondrously. Among voices are those that gladden, those that put to sleep, those that make one laugh and rejoice, and those that draw from the limbs movements in time with them, of the hand, foot and head. One should not suppose that this is from understanding the meanings of the poetry; rather it also holds for strings, so that it has been said: whoever is not moved by spring and its flowers, nor by the lute and its strings, has a corrupt temperament that has no cure. How could it be from understanding the meaning, when its effect is observed in the infant in his cradle, whom a good voice stills from his crying, and his soul turns from what makes him cry to listening to it? And the camel, despite the dullness of its nature, is affected by the ḥudāʾ so that heavy loads become light for it and, through the vigour of its delight in listening, long distances seem short; there arises in it a gaiety that intoxicates and bewilders it. You see camels, when the deserts have been long for them and weariness and exhaustion come over them under their litters and loads, when they hear the caller of the ḥudāʾ, stretch out their necks, listening to the driver with ears pricked, and hasten their pace until their loads and litters are shaken upon them, and perhaps they destroy themselves by the hardness of the going and the weight of the load without feeling it because of their gaiety." Then al-Ghazālī mentioned, as proof of what he said, the story of the slave who destroyed the camels by the sweetness of his voice, when he made them cover a three-day journey in a single night, and after that he said: "The effect of samāʿ on the heart is felt, and whoever is not moved by samāʿ is deficient, inclined away from moderation, far from spirituality, exceeding camels and birds, indeed all beasts, in coarseness and density of nature, for all of them are affected by measured melodies. For this reason the birds used to stand over the head of Dāwūd, peace be upon him, to listen to his voice. And whenever the consideration of samāʿ is with regard to its effect on the heart, it is in no way permissible to judge it as lawful or forbidden absolutely, but that differs according to circumstances, persons and the differing ways of melodies; so its ruling is the ruling of what is in the heart."
Among the strange things transmitted about the effect of song: The singer Mukhāriq went out with some of his companions to one of the pleasure-grounds, and saw a gilded bow with one of those who had come out with him, and asked him for it. The one asked seemed to be niggardly with it. Gazelles passed near him on the right, and he said to the owner of the bow: "Do you think that if I sang a song and the cheeks of these gazelles turned toward you, you would hand me this bow?" He said yes. So he launched into singing:
ماذا تقول الظباء ... أفرقة أم لقاء؟
أم عهدها بسليمى ... وفي البيان شفاء
مرت بنا سانحات ... وقد دنا الإمساء
فما أحارت جوابا ... وطال فيها الغناء
(What do the gazelles say: parting or meeting? Or is it their covenant with Sulaymā? In clear speech there is healing. They passed us on our right as evening drew near; they gave no answer, and the song about them grew long.)
The gazelles turned back toward him until they stopped near him, craning to look at him and listening to his voice. Those present marvelled at their returning and standing, and the man handed him the bow. He took it and cut off the song, and the gazelles resumed their flight and went back on their course.
The story of the pretty woman in the black veil:
The story of the pretty woman in the black veil is well known and is among the best of what is cited as an example. Al-Aṣmaʿī relates it, saying: "A bedouin came with a bale of Iraqi veils and sold them all except the black ones, and complained of that to al-Dārimī (that is Miskīn al-Dārimī the poet), who had become devout, had left poetry and kept to the mosque. He said: What will you give me, if I contrive a trick for you until you sell them all at your own price? He said: Whatever you wish. So al-Dārimī went to his clothes of devotion, threw them off, returned to his former state, composed a poem and gave it to a friend of his among the singers, who sang it. The poem was:
قل للمليحة في الخمار الأسود ... ماذا فعلت بناسك متعبّد
قد كان شمر للصلاة ثيابه ... حتى خطرت له بباب المسجد
ردّي عليه صلاته وصيامه ... لا تقتليه بحق دين محمد
(Say to the pretty one in the black veil: what have you done to a devout worshipper? He had hitched up his garments for prayer, until you sauntered before him at the door of the mosque. Give him back his prayer and his fasting; do not kill him, by the right of the religion of Muḥammad.)
This song spread in Medina and they said: al-Dārimī has returned and fallen in love with the woman of the black veil. So no pretty woman remained in Medina without buying a black veil, and the merchant sold everything he had with him. The brothers of al-Dārimī among the devout began to pass by and say: What have you done? He would say: You will know in a while. When the Iraqi had sold everything he had with him, al-Dārimī returned to his devotion and put on his clothes."
Were we to wish to exhaust what has been reported in this chapter of wondrous effect, our discussion would grow long, but we have contented ourselves with what we have cited so as not to depart from the subject.

dervis-irab:51-54.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath and has entered upon the conditional particle. أرسلنا is a verb and agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and ريحا is the object of أرسلنا. فرأوه is conjoined to أرسلنا, and consists of a verb, agent and direct object; مصفرا is a ḥāl. ولظلوا: the lām occurs in the response to the oath; ظلوا is a defective past verb and the wāw is its noun; the sentence has no grammatical position because it is the response to the oath, and it has made the apodosis of the condition unnecessary, according to the well-known rule:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم
(When a condition and an oath come together, omit the response of the one you put later; it is the one retained.) من بعده is a ḥāl, and the clause يكفرون is the predicate of ظلوا. (فَإِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتى وَلا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ إِذا وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ) The fāʾ is causal, and the sentence gives the reason for an omitted element, i.e. "do not be distressed and do not grieve at their lack of belief, for they are dead, deaf and blind". inna and its noun, and the clause لا تسمع الموتى is its predicate; ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء is conjoined to the preceding sentence; الصم is the first object of تسمع and الدعاء the second object of تسمع; إذا is an adverb of future time attached to تسمع, and the clause ولوا is that to which the adverb is annexed; ولوا is a verb and agent, and مدبرين is a ḥāl from the wāw.
(وَما أَنْتَ بِهادِي الْعُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is the Ḥijāzī negative, أنت its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and هادي is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the predicate of ما; العمي is a muḍāf ilayhi; عن ضلالتهم is attached to العمي or to هادي, by endowing هادي with the sense of "diverter"; its like has been given before.
(إِنْ تُسْمِعُ إِلَّا مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنا فَهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ) إن is negative, تسمع is an imperfect verb in the nominative whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; إلا is a particle of restriction, من is a direct object, the clause يؤمن is the ṣila of من, and بآياتنا is attached to يؤمن. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction by sense; هم is the subject and مسلمون the predicate. (اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ) الله is the subject, الذي the predicate, the clause خلقكم the ṣila, and من ضعف is attached to خلقكم.
(ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً) ثم is a particle of conjunction and delay; جعل is a past verb; من بعد ضعف is the second object of جعل, or is attached to جعل; and قوة is the object of جعل.
(ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفاً وَشَيْبَةً يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَدِيرُ) ثم and what follows is conjoined to what precedes, and the clause يخلق ما يشاء is circumstantial; هو is the subject, العليم the first predicate and القدير the second predicate.

dervis-irab:55-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّاعَةُ): the Resurrection, so named because it will arise in the last hour of the hours of this world, or because it will occur suddenly and unexpectedly; it has become a proper name for it, like al-najm for the Pleiades and al-kawkab for Venus. In al-Qāmūs: "al-sāʿa is one of the parts of the night and day, and the present time; the plural is sāʿāt and sāʿ; and the Resurrection, or the time in which the Resurrection arises; and the perishing, like al-jāʿa for al-jiyāʿ." Al-sāʿa also means an instrument (a later usage) by which time is known according to hours, among them the sand-glass (sāʿa ramliyya) and the sundial (sāʿa shamsiyya).
(يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ): they are asked for al-ʿutbā, i.e. return, from your saying "so-and-so asked me to appease him (istaʿtabanī) and I appeased him (aʿtabtuhu)", i.e. he sought my satisfaction and I satisfied him; that is when you were the wrongdoer against him; and the reality of aʿtabtuhu is that I removed his reproach. Do you not see His words:
غضبت تميم أن تقتل عامرا ... يوم النسار فأعتبوا بالصيلم
(Tamīm were angry that ʿĀmir was killed on the day of al-Nisār, so they were appeased by al-Ṣaylam.) How he made them angry and then said "so they were appeased", i.e. their anger was removed; anger is in the sense of reproach. Al-Ṣaylam is a water of the Banū ʿĀmir, and al-ṣaylam is also calamity and the sword, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ʿataba ʿalayhi ʿatban, of the patterns ḍaraba and qatala, and muʿtaban also: he blamed him in anger, so he is ʿātib, and ʿattāb, an intensive; from it comes the name ʿAttāb ibn Asīd; and ʿātabahu muʿātabatan and ʿitāban. Al-Khalīl said: the reality of ʿitāb is an address of presumption and a discussion of displeasure. Aʿtabanī: the hamza is for deprivation, i.e. he removed the complaint and the reproach; istaʿtaba: he sought the removal of reproach; and al-ʿutbā is a noun from iʿtāb."
(يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ): let them not carry you to levity and rashness through abandoning patience.

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ) The adverb is attached to يقسم, and the clause تقوم الساعة is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. يقسم المجرمون is a verb and agent; ما is negative; لبثوا is a verb and agent, and the sentence has no grammatical position because it occurs in the response to the oath; and غير ساعة is an adverbial attached to لبثوا.
(كَذلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "they are turned away from the truth, which is the veracity, as they were turned away from the truth, which is the Resurrection"; kāna and its noun, and the clause يؤفكون is its predicate; يؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ وَالْإِيمانَ لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ إِلى يَوْمِ الْبَعْثِ) The wāw is a conjunction; وقال الذين is a verb and agent, the clause أوتوا is the ṣila, العلم is the second object of أوتوا, and الإيمان is conjoined to العلم. The sentence لقد لبثتم is the content of the saying. The lām is a response to an omitted oath, قد is a particle of certainty, لبثتم is a verb and agent, في كتاب الله is a ḥāl, i.e. "reckoned in Allah's knowledge and decree", and إلى يوم البعث is attached to لبثتم. (فَهذا يَوْمُ الْبَعْثِ وَلكِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa because it discloses an implied condition, as if he said: "if you were deniers of the Resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection", i.e. the falsity of your statement has become evident. ولكنكم: the wāw is circumstantial; lākinna and its noun; the clause كنتم is its predicate, and the clause لا تعلمون is the predicate of كنتم.
(فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يَنْفَعُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ) The fāʾ is for detailing what precedes it, which is understood from the shortening of the period of stay, so it is also a fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like and attached to ينفع, and the tanwīn is a substitute for an omitted sentence, i.e. "the day when the Hour arose, the polytheists swore falsely, and those given knowledge and faith, angels and others, answered them". لا is negative, ينفع is an imperfect verb, الذين ظلموا is its fronted object, and معذرتهم is the agent of ينفع. It was read ينفع with yāʾ and with tāʾ because معذرتهم is of non-real feminine gender, or has the sense of "excuse". The wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, هم is the subject, the clause يستعتبون is the predicate, and يستعتبون is a passive imperfect verb whose wāw is the deputy agent.
(وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ) The wāw is resumptive, the lām prepares for the oath, قد is a particle of certainty, and للناس is attached to ضربنا. في هذا القرآن is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; من كل مثل is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. an admonition or a story from every parable; or من may be partitive and the preposition and its genitive noun be in the position of the accusative as the object of ضربنا, i.e. "We described to them every description, as if it were a parable in its strangeness and novelty".
(وَلَئِنْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ لَيَقُولَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا مُبْطِلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath, and إن is conditional; جئتهم is a verb, agent and direct object in the position of the protasis, and بآية is attached to جئتهم. ليقولن: the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, so the lām is fatḥa-voweled by agreement of the readers; the agent is the relative noun, by way of putting the overt in place of the pronoun, which has been mentioned many times. The clause كفروا is the ṣila. إن is negative, أنتم the subject, إلا a particle of restriction, and مبطلون the predicate of أنتم, and the sentence is the content of the saying. (كَذلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "in the like of that sealing, Allah seals the hearts of the ignorant who do not know", and the clause لا يعلمون is the ṣila of الذين.
(فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ الَّذِينَ لا يُوقِنُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you have known that their state is of this standing, then be patient". اصبر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", and the clause إن وعد الله حق gives the reason for the command to be patient. ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; يستخفنك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive by the prohibitive lā; the kāf is a fronted direct object, and الذين is the postponed agent of يستخفنك; the clause لا يوقنون is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة» there is perfect jinās (jinās tāmm). The discussion of this art has preceded, and we now want to complete its discussions, for it has many kinds, among them al-māthila, which is that the word is one with a different meaning, such as the saying of Ziyād al-Aʿjam, and it was said al-Ṣaltān al-ʿAbdī, lamenting al-Mughīra ibn al-Muhallab:
فانع المغيرة للمغيرة إذ بدت ... شعواء مشعلة كنبح النابح
(Announce al-Mughīra's death to the mounted raiders when a widespread, blazing raid appeared, like the barking of a barker.) The first «المغيرة» is a man, and the second «المغيرة» is the horse, which is the second of the horses that raid. Abū Nuwās said about Ibn al-Rabīʿ:
عباس عباس إذا احتدم الوغى ... والفضل فضل والربيع ربيع
(ʿAbbās is a lion when battle blazes, and al-Faḍl is Faḍl, and al-Rabīʿ is spring.) And Abū Tammām said:
ليالينا بالرقمتين وأهلنا ... سقى العهد منك العهد والعهد والعهد
(Our nights at the two Raqmas, and our people: may the age of you be watered by the rain, the covenant and the bond.) The first ʿahd, that which is watered, is the time; the second ʿahd is protective loyalty, from their saying "so-and-so has no ʿahd"; the third ʿahd is a bequest, from their saying "so-and-so bequeathed to so-and-so", and "I bequeathed to him", i.e. he charged me and I charged him; and the fourth ʿahd is rain, and its plural is ʿihād. Some people found this paronomasia heavy, and rightly so.
Abū Tammām was extremely fond of paronomasia; he did well in some and fell short in the rest, and we have given earlier in this book examples of his successes and failures; the affectation in it is plainly visible.
As for Ibn al-Rūmī, he was not among the enthusiasts for verbal craft and did not busy himself much with wording. He made paronomasia only for a meaning he saw, and did not make it for empty adornment and foolish diversion. Among his fine examples:
للسود في السود آثار تركن بها ... لمعا من البيض تثني أعين البيض
(The black ones have left traces upon the black ones, glimmers of white that turn aside the eyes of the fair ones.) The first «السود» are the nights; the other «السود» are the hairs of the head and beard; the first «البيض» are the grey hairs and the other «البيض» are the women.
And his saying:
فيسبيك بالسحر الذي في جفونه ... ويصبيك بالسحر الذي هو نافثه
(He captivates you with the magic in his eyelids, and enchants you with the magic he breathes out.)
Or like this verse:
تصيب إذا حكمت وإن طلبنا ... لديك العرف كنت حيا تصوب
(You hit the mark when you judge, and if we seek kindness from you, you were a rain that pours down.)
Or like this verse:
ليس ينفكّ طيرها في اصطحاب ... تحت أظلال أيكها واصطخاب
(Its birds never cease to be together, under the shades of its thicket, in clamour.)
Thus it was in all his paronomasia, with no excess in it, and it is not frequently prominent in his large divan. When he makes paronomasia otherwise, he is playing, deliberately playing, not stitching together embellishments nor seeking adornment, as he said:
لو تلفّفت في كساء الكسائي ... وتلبّست فروة الفرّاء
وتخلّلت بالخليل وأضحى ... سيبويه لديك رهن سباء
وتكوّنت من سواد أبي الاسو ... د شخصا يكنى أبا السوداء
(If you wrapped yourself in the cloak of al-Kisāʾī, and put on the fur of al-Farrāʾ; and wore al-Khalīl as your inner garment, and Sībawayh became your captive; and were made from the blackness of Abū l-Aswad a person called Abū l-Sawdāʾ,) Allah would refuse that people of learning should count you except among the dull-witted.
Among the scholars of rhetoric are those who gave it a name by which they called it, al-taradīd (repetition), meaning that the one word is repeated in it; it is when the poet brings a word attached to one meaning and then repeats the very same word attached to another meaning in the same verse or part of it. Abū Tammām said:
خفّت دموعك في إثر القطين لدن ... خفّت من الكثب القضبان والكثب
(Your tears grew scant after the departure of the tribe, when they moved lightly from the dunes, the branches and the dunes.) The taradīd is in «خفّت»; and if you made «الكثب» the taradīd, it would be permissible.
And Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī said, and excelled as he wished:
أمير أمير عليه الندى ... جواد بخيل بأن لا يجودا
(A prince, a prince over whom generosity rules; generous, yet miserly at not giving.) The taradīd is at the beginning of the verse. The scholars of poetry agree on the precedence of Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī in his words:
ألا حيّ من أجل الحبيب المغانيا ... لبسن البلى مما لبسن اللياليا
إذا ما تقاضى المرء يوما وليلة ... تقاضاه شيء لا يملّ التقاضيا
(Greet, for the sake of the beloved, the abodes, which have put on decay from what the nights have put on. When a man demands for a day and a night, something presses him that never tires of pressing.)
How beautiful is the saying of Abū Nuwās:
دع عنك لومي فإن اللوم إغراء ... وداوني بالتي كانت هي الداء
صفراء لا تنزل الأكدار ساحتها ... لو مسها حجر مستها سراء
(Leave off blaming me, for blame is incitement; and cure me with that which was itself the disease. A yellow one, whose courtyard troubles do not enter; were a stone to touch it, gladness would touch it.)
And likewise the saying of Abū Tammām:
راح إذا ما الراح كنّ مطيّها ... كانت مطايا الشوق في الأحشاء
(Wine, such that when the wines are its mounts, the mounts of longing are in the entrails.) He repeated «مطيّها» and «مطايا الشوق».
Returning to the noble verse, we mention that Ibn Abī l-Ḥadīd, in his book called al-Falak al-Dāʾir ʿalā l-Mathal al-Sāʾir, disputed this and said:
The meaning in the verse is one, for the Day of Resurrection, though long, is with Allah the Exalted like one hour with any one of us; and then applying "hour" to it is figurative, as in our saying "I saw a lion" and "Zayd is a lion", where by the first we meant the animal and by the second the brave man.
We have not seen anyone disputing what we mentioned except Ibn Abī l-Ḥadīd; so ponder.

dervis-irab:17-22.t:
* I'rab:
(فَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ), as though it clarified and made explicit what preceded of His greatness in creation, its beginning, and the rising of the Hour as its end: so when that has become clear to you, glorify Allah and praise Him in every state, because tasbīḥ (glorification) and taqdīs (sanctification) are the two means to salvation. It is also said that He pointed to the five prayers in this verse, for it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, when he was asked: "Do you find the five prayers in the Qur'an?", that he said: "Yes", and recited this verse. In تمسون are the two prayers maghrib and ʿishāʾ; in تصبحون is the dawn prayer; in العشي is the afternoon prayer; and in تظهرون is the noon prayer, i.e. you enter the midday. سبحان الله is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; حين تمسون is an adverb attached to سبحان, and the clause تمسون is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; تمسون is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is fāʿil (agent), because it is complete (tāmma), its meaning being "you enter the evening"; the discussion of completeness will come in the chapter on benefits. وحين تصبحون is conjoined to حين تمسون. (وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ) The wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined; there is a point in it which al-Rāzī mentioned and which will come in the chapter on benefits. له is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الحمد a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); في السموات is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and الأرض is conjoined to السموات; the sentence is parenthetical. وعشيا is conjoined to حين تمسون, and likewise his saying وحين تظهرون. (يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ) The sentence is resumptive or circumstantial; يخرج is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to Allah; الحي is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and من الميت is attached to يخرج, i.e. like the human being from the sperm-drop and the bird from the egg; ويخرج الميت من الحي is conjoined to what precedes, i.e. like the sperm-drop from the human being and the egg from the bird.
(وَيُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها وَكَذلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ويحيي الأرض is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the adverb بعد موتها is attached to يحيي, and its giving life is the bringing forth of plants from it; وكذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you will be brought forth in the like of that bringing forth"; تخرجون is an imperfect passive verb and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); it has been read in the active, in which case the wāw is fāʿil.
(وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ إِذا أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ تَنْتَشِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, من آياته is a fronted khabar, and أن with what is within its scope is a delayed mubtadaʾ; من تراب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقكم; ثم is a conjunction of delay; إذا is the sudden (fujāʾiyya) إذا; أنتم is mubtadaʾ and بشر is khabar, and the clause تنتشرون is a ḥāl; the occurrence of the sudden إذا after ثم will come in the chapter on benefits. (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْواجاً لِتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْها)
The wāw is a conjunction and the sentence is conjoined to the one before it; and He, Glorified, has mentioned six of His signs. أزواجا is mafʿūl bihi of خلق; the lām is for giving a reason; تسكنوا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and إليها is attached to تسكنوا. (وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ مَوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ) وجعل is conjoined to خلق; بينكم is an adverb in the position of the second mafʿūl of جعل, and مودة is the first mafʿūl; رحمة is conjoined to مودة; إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, and في ذلك is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and آيات is its delayed ism; لقوم is an adjective of آيات, and the clause يتفكرون is an adjective of قوم.
(وَمِنْ آياتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلافُ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَلْوانِكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِلْعالِمِينَ) Also conjoined to what preceded; the wisdom of the difference between tongues and colours will come in the chapter on benefits.

* Benefits:
